questions.question: How do the official docs define Next.js?
options: A React framework for building full-stack web applications
questions.explanation: The docs' first sentence: a React framework for building full-stack web applications.

questions.question: React is best described as…
options: a library for building user interfaces
questions.explanation: React turns components into UI; it leaves routing, data and serving to other tools.

questions.question: Is every Next.js app a React app?
options: Only if you use the Pages Router
Yes: you write React components, Next.js adds the framework around them
No: Next.js uses its own component model
questions.explanation: Next.js builds on React; everything you know about components, props and hooks still applies.

questions.question: What does a typical Vite + React single-page app send as its first HTML?
options: An almost empty page with a root div and a script tag
questions.explanation: JavaScript builds the page in the browser, so the HTML is nearly empty.

questions.question: By default, components in the app folder are…
questions.explanation: Every component in app/ is a Server Component unless its file (or an importer) says "use client".

questions.question: Which problems does server-rendered HTML help with? (select all that apply)
options: A blank screen while JavaScript loads
Slow phones having to build the page themselves
Making client-side state persist across reloads
Search engines and link previews reading content
questions.explanation: HTML with content arrives before any JavaScript runs; state persistence is unrelated.

questions.question: What does "full-stack" mean in the docs' definition?
options: Pages, data access and an API live in one project
questions.explanation: Route Handlers and Server Functions let one Next.js project cover front end and back end.

questions.question: Which statement about Client Components is true?
options: They never run on the server
They are sent to the browser as HTML only
They are prerendered to HTML on the server, then hydrated in the browser
questions.explanation: Client Components render on the server too; hydration makes them interactive.

questions.question: What is hydration?
options: React attaching event handlers to server-rendered HTML so it becomes interactive
questions.explanation: Hydration makes the static HTML preview interactive.

questions.question: In Next.js 16 with Cache Components, what does Partial Prerendering mean?
options: A prerendered static shell with dynamic parts streamed in through Suspense
Only half of the routes are prerendered
Client Components are skipped during the build
questions.explanation: The static shell is sent instantly; request-dependent parts stream in.

questions.question: Which older rendering term corresponds to content built once at build time?
questions.explanation: Static site generation: prerendered at build time.

questions.question: Which older term corresponds to rendering HTML on the server for each request?
questions.explanation: Server-side rendering per request; in Next.js 16, dynamic rendering.

questions.question: ISR (incremental static regeneration) maps to which Next.js 16 feature?
options: Cached data with cacheLife, refreshed in the background or by tags
questions.explanation: Cached results are regenerated after a time or an event.

questions.question: Do you need to deploy Next.js to Vercel?
options: Yes, it only runs on Vercel
No: next build and next start run on any Node.js server
questions.explanation: Vercel hosts it well, but self-hosting, Docker and adapters work too.

questions.question: For which project would plain React + Vite usually be enough? (select all that apply)
options: An in-browser image editor with no SEO needs
A blog with hundreds of articles
An internal admin panel that calls an existing API
questions.explanation: Client-only tools without SEO needs don't gain much from server rendering.

questions.question: Which are good reasons to choose Next.js? (select all that apply)
options: One TypeScript codebase for front end and API
You need a long-running job queue
Public pages that must load fast and rank in search
questions.explanation: Job queues belong in a dedicated back end; the others are Next.js strengths.

questions.question: A teammate says "we'll use Next.js so we don't need a back end". When is that most clearly wrong?
options: When you need long-running jobs, queues or an API shared by many clients and teams
questions.explanation: Next.js covers request/response server code; long-running work and big shared APIs deserve their own service.

questions.question: Which router does this book (and the docs for new apps) use?
questions.explanation: The App Router supports Server Components, streaming and Server Functions.

questions.question: Why don't Server Components add to the browser's JavaScript bundle?
options: They are cached in the browser
Only their rendered result is sent, not their code
They run in a web worker
questions.explanation: Their code runs on the server; the browser receives HTML and the RSC payload.

questions.question: What is a request waterfall in a client-rendered app?
options: Fetches that start one after another because each waits for a render or another fetch
questions.explanation: load JS → render → fetch → render → fetch… each step waits for the previous.

questions.question: Why are secrets safer in Server Components than in a client-side React app?
options: The code that uses them runs only on the server; only the result is sent
Secrets are deleted after the build
questions.explanation: Server code and its credentials never reach the browser bundle (unless you pass them as props).

questions.question: What is a Route Handler?
options: A route.ts file that answers HTTP requests with Request and Response
questions.explanation: Route Handlers are API endpoints in the app folder.

questions.question: What happens when you open a Client Component's page with JavaScript disabled?
options: You see its prerendered HTML, but clicks do nothing
questions.explanation: The HTML exists; interactivity needs hydration.

questions.question: Which of these lets the server, not the browser, talk to the database? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Server Components, Server Functions and Route Handlers run on the server.

questions.question: In the analogy of this book, React is the engine and Next.js is…
options: the complete car built around it
questions.explanation: A framework provides the rest of the car around the React engine.

questions.question: Who calls your page component in a framework like Next.js?
options: The framework, when a URL is requested
questions.explanation: A framework calls your code at the right places; a library is called by you.

questions.question: Which tasks does Next.js configure for you that you'd otherwise assemble with plain React? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The framework handles infrastructure; your app logic is still yours.

questions.question: Which statement about Next.js and SEO is accurate?
options: Client Components are invisible to search engines
Content and metadata are in the HTML, which crawlers and link previews read
Next.js submits your site to Google automatically
questions.explanation: Server-rendered HTML and the Metadata API are the SEO benefits; Client Components are also prerendered.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT something Next.js adds on top of React?
questions.explanation: Components and hooks are React itself. See Chapter 1, What Next.js Is (and Isn't).

questions.question: Which are part of what the book calls 'full-stack' in one Next.js project? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Pages, data and API share one codebase. See Chapter 1, What Next.js Is (and Isn't).

questions.question: Which statement about Next.js and React versions is right?
options: The App Router uses React canary features bundled with Next.js; you still list react in package.json
questions.explanation: From the docs' React version handling section.

questions.question: What does 'code splitting' mean in Next.js?
options: Splitting files into server and client folders
Each route loads only the JavaScript it needs
questions.explanation: Automatic per-route bundles. See Chapter 1, What Next.js Is (and Isn't).

questions.question: Which is a framework?
questions.explanation: React, Lodash and Zod are libraries. See Chapter 1, What Next.js Is (and Isn't).

questions.question: In the bakery analogy, partial prerendering is…
options: a fresh batch when the old one gets stale
a sandwich made entirely to order
a sandwich on bread baked this morning, filled while you watch
questions.explanation: Static shell + personal part now. See Chapter 1, What Next.js Is (and Isn't).

questions.question: Your product page shows a description (weekly changes) and a price from a cookie-based country. How does Next.js 16 render it?
options: Description in the cached static shell; price streamed per request in Suspense
The whole page at build time
questions.explanation: Partial prerendering. See Chapter 1, What Next.js Is (and Isn't).

questions.question: Where does a static Server Component's console.log appear in production?
options: In the build output (it runs during next build)
questions.explanation: Static pages render at build time. See Chapter 1, What Next.js Is (and Isn't).

questions.question: What does 'prerendered' mean?
options: Rendered ahead of time (at build or revalidation) and stored
questions.explanation: Served instantly afterwards. See Chapter 1, What Next.js Is (and Isn't).

questions.question: Which needs does Next.js NOT cover out of the box?
options: A message queue for background jobs
questions.explanation: Use a dedicated service for queues. See Chapter 1, What Next.js Is (and Isn't).

questions.question: What does 'Backend for Frontend' mean in the docs?
options: Next.js acts as the web front end's server layer, calling other back-end services
questions.explanation: A guide in the docs. See Chapter 1, What Next.js Is (and Isn't).

questions.question: Why does Next.js send both HTML and an RSC payload on first load?
options: HTML for an instant preview; the payload so React can rebuild the tree and hydrate
questions.explanation: From Chapter 5. See Chapter 1, What Next.js Is (and Isn't).

questions.question: Where do you import `NextConfig` from (type)?
questions.explanation: NextConfig comes from next. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: What is the `next.config.ts` file for?
options: The Pages Router component that wraps every page
An error boundary (a Client Component) for a route segment
Local environment variables, loaded into process.env and never committed
questions.explanation: next.config.ts: The Next.js configuration file.

questions.question: Which file convention is this? "The Next.js configuration file"
questions.explanation: The Next.js configuration file: that's next.config.ts.

questions.question: What is the `next-env.d.ts` file for?
options: A register() function that runs once when a server instance starts
The fallback for a parallel route slot
Generated TypeScript declarations for Next.js (not edited or committed)
Like a layout, but re-mounted on every navigation
questions.explanation: next-env.d.ts: Generated TypeScript declarations for Next.js (not edited or committed).

questions.question: Which file convention is this? "Generated TypeScript declarations for Next.js (not edited or committed)"
questions.explanation: Generated TypeScript declarations for Next.js (not edited or committed): that's next-env.d.ts.

questions.question: What does `next dev` do?
options: Start the development server with Fast Refresh
Create a production build: compile, type-check, prerender, print the route table
Run the Vitest unit tests once (not in watch mode)
questions.explanation: next dev: Start the development server with Fast Refresh.

questions.question: What does `next build` do?
options: Print system and package versions for bug reports
Create a production build: compile, type-check, prerender, print the route table
Generate route types (PageProps, LayoutProps) without a full build
questions.explanation: next build: Create a production build: compile, type-check, prerender, print the route table.

questions.question: What does `next start` do?
options: Generate route types (PageProps, LayoutProps) without a full build
Print system and package versions for bug reports
Create a production build: compile, type-check, prerender, print the route table
questions.explanation: next start: Serve the production build. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: What does `next typegen` do?
options: Print system and package versions for bug reports
Run the Vitest unit tests once (not in watch mode)
Generate route types (PageProps, LayoutProps) without a full build
questions.explanation: next typegen: Generate route types (PageProps, LayoutProps) without a full build.

questions.question: What does `next info` do?
options: Upgrade Next.js and React to the latest version
Create a new app with the recommended defaults
Print system and package versions for bug reports
questions.explanation: next info: Print system and package versions for bug reports.

questions.question: What does `npx create-next-app@latest my-app --yes` do?
options: Print system and package versions for bug reports
Run the Vitest unit tests once (not in watch mode)
Create a new app with the recommended defaults
questions.explanation: npx create-next-app@latest my-app --yes: Create a new app with the recommended defaults.

questions.question: What is the minimum Node.js version for Next.js 16?
questions.explanation: The Installation page lists Node.js 20.9 as the minimum.

questions.question: What does create-next-app --yes do?
options: Uses the recommended defaults (or saved preferences) without asking
questions.explanation: --yes skips the prompts. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: Which are enabled by create-next-app's recommended defaults? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The default line: TypeScript, ESLint, No React Compiler, Tailwind CSS, No src/, App Router, Cache Components, AGENTS.md.

questions.question: Is a src/ directory used by the recommended defaults?
questions.explanation: No src/ directory is part of the defaults.

questions.question: Where are the docs for your exact installed Next.js version?
questions.explanation: The next package ships its docs; AGENTS.md points agents there.

questions.question: Which bundler does next dev use by default in Next.js 16?
questions.explanation: Turbopack is the default; --webpack switches back.

questions.question: Since Next.js 16, does next build run the linter?
options: No: run eslint yourself (npm run lint)
questions.explanation: next lint was removed; next build no longer lints.

questions.question: Which two files must an App Router app have at minimum?
options: app/layout.tsx and a page such as app/page.tsx
questions.explanation: A root layout with html and body, and at least one page.

questions.question: What must the root layout render?
questions.explanation: The root layout is required and must contain html and body.

questions.question: What does next dev skip that next build does? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Dev strips types without checking and renders on each request.

questions.question: A file at public/robots.txt is served at…
questions.explanation: Files in public/ are served from the site root.

questions.question: What happens if public/about.txt and app/about.txt/page.tsx both exist (as tested in the book)?
options: The build fails with a conflict
The build succeeds, but /about.txt serves the public file and the page is unreachable
questions.explanation: The book tested this with 16.4.5: no warning, the public file wins.

questions.question: What does the @/* alias in tsconfig.json do?
options: Lets you import from the project root, e.g. @/lib/books
questions.explanation: paths: { "@/*": ["./*"] }. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: What is next-env.d.ts?
options: Generated TypeScript declarations for Next.js; don't edit or commit it
questions.explanation: It's generated and should be kept out of git.

questions.question: Which statement about cacheComponents: true in next.config.ts is correct?
options: Data is dynamic unless cached with "use cache", and every route gets a static shell
questions.explanation: Cache Components is the model of Chapters 6–9.

questions.question: What does partialPrefetching: true do?
options: Lets <Link> prefetch each route's static shell
questions.explanation: Partial Prefetching prefetches App Shells of linked routes.

questions.question: A build fails with "app/page.tsx(4,26): error TS2345: Argument of type 'string' is not assignable…". What do 4 and 26 mean?
questions.explanation: file(line,column): error TScode: message.

questions.question: If you use a src/ folder, which of these stay at the project root? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: app/ moves into src/; config, env files and public stay at the root.

questions.question: What does next typegen do?
options: Generates route types like PageProps without a full build
questions.explanation: Handy in CI before running tsc. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: Why does the book say to build and start the app often while developing?
options: Builds are required to save files
Type errors and prerendering rules only show up in a production build
questions.explanation: Dev mode hides build-only problems. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a Next.js file convention?
questions.explanation: lib/ is just a common folder name. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: How can you make VS Code tell same-named page.tsx tabs apart, as the docs suggest?
questions.explanation: workbench.editor.customLabels.patterns shows folder names in tab labels.

questions.question: Without a tsconfig.json, what happens when you add a .tsx file and run next dev?
options: Next.js installs TypeScript and writes a recommended tsconfig.json
questions.explanation: Next.js sets up TypeScript automatically.

questions.question: What is AGENTS.md for?
options: Instructions for AI coding agents, pointing them at the bundled docs
questions.explanation: create-next-app includes it to help agents write up-to-date code.

questions.question: Which statement about the generated next.config.ts's turbopack.rules entry is right?
options: It runs CSS files through Tailwind's Turbopack loader
questions.explanation: The *.css rule uses @tailwindcss/turbopack.

questions.question: Which ports does next start use by default, and how do you change it?
questions.explanation: -p sets the port for dev and start. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: What do the four create-next-app scripts run? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Plus eslint for lint. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: Why is skipLibCheck: true and noEmit: true in the generated tsconfig?
options: Skip checking library types for speed; TypeScript only checks, Next.js compiles
questions.explanation: noEmit: Next.js (Turbopack) does the compiling.

questions.question: Which linters can create-next-app set up?
questions.explanation: ESLint is the default. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: What does npm run dev print as the local address by default?
questions.explanation: Port 3000. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: Which TypeScript version does Next.js require at minimum?
questions.explanation: From the Installation page. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: What is the /_not-found route in the route table?
questions.explanation: Customise it with not-found.tsx. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.

questions.question: What does the Network address in next dev's output allow?
options: Opening the dev server from other devices on your network
questions.explanation: e.g. testing on your phone. See Chapter 2, Installation & Project Structure.
